Did Carl Jung ever study or develop an Archetypal Understanding of the "Scientist?" In some fundamental sense, Jung himself, being a Psychoanalyst, would definitely be considered "a Scientist of Human behavior and nature" moreso than his Esoteric explorations of the Divine, Sacred and Metaphysical... which is just as important... and perhaps, I argue; Integral to the Scientist.

A purely materialistic, deterministic, world is somewhat indistinguishable from the automaton; the Scientist's achilles' heel, in some fundamental sense, is desensitization to the mundane; ironically, studying it at microscopic and macroscopic scales, one analyzes and intellectualizes what is not purely of the intellectual realm.

That's my interpretation anyway, hopefully it is not too far off from the Empirical, Collective understanding of the Logical, Analytical, Scienfitic-oriented Individual... and more importantly; how to integrate the vast, Volatile faculties of the Intellect, the Rational mind, the Sciences and the Real-world... such that both the Mundane and the Sacred are not crushed by the Profane[^2]

Science has the power of machines; to cure disease or to cause it. To be the effect of positive change, or the cause of societal collapse. Science, Theology (excluding the Dogmatic aspect of Religions, the Harmful Ideaolgies and the Corrosive Philosophies...) and the Human Phenomenology (what a Human Being experiences 1:1 with Reality) must work together; These Domains must Unify and Integrate[^1]

[^1]: Which was Jung's Brilliant concept of "Individuation" as a necessary stage of Psychological, Humane Transformation.

[^2]: ...a reference to Mircae Eliade's work.
